blocks.markdown:
Today's big question: what do plants need to grow?

We will grow cress and be plant detectives.
blocks.say: Welcome back, young scientist! Today's big question is: what do plants need to grow? By the end, you will name the parts of a plant, watch a seed grow, and plan a fair test with cress. Let's go!

blocks.alt: Plants come in all shapes and sizes.
blocks.caption: Plants come in all shapes and sizes.

terms.meaning: Living things that grow in soil and make their own food.

blocks.text: Stop 1: Roots, stem, leaves and flower

blocks.markdown:
A plant has **roots**, a **stem**, **leaves** and a **flower**.

Each part has a job.
blocks.say: A plant has four main parts, and each has a job. The roots grow down in the soil. They hold the plant still and drink up water. The stem holds the plant up and carries water to every part. The leaves catch sunlight to make food. And the flower makes seeds. Let's look at each part.

scenes.caption: Roots drink water.
scenes.say: The roots are under the soil. They drink water and hold the plant steady.

scenes.caption: The stem holds the plant up.
scenes.say: The stem holds the plant up. Water travels up inside it, like a straw.

scenes.caption: Leaves catch light.
scenes.say: The leaves are green. They catch sunlight, and the plant uses it to make food.

scenes.caption: The flower makes seeds.
scenes.say: The flower makes seeds, so that new plants can grow.

question.prompt: Which part of a plant drinks water from the soil?
question.hint: It grows down in the soil.
question.explanation: Roots take in water from the soil.

blocks.alt: A tree, a daisy and a date palm.
blocks.caption: A tree, a daisy and a date palm.
blocks.say: Trees have all the same parts, only bigger. The trunk is the tree's stem, and it is very thick and strong. Plants come in many shapes: tall trees, little daisies and juicy fruit trees, like the mango and the date palm.

blocks.markdown: A tree's **trunk** is its big, strong stem.
blocks.say: Trees are plants too. Their trunk is just a thick, woody stem.

question.hint: It has roots, a stem and leaves.
question.explanation: Trees are plants with a very thick stem called a trunk.

points: Roots take in water and hold the plant
The stem holds the plant up

blocks.say: Remember. Roots drink and hold, the stem holds up, leaves catch light and the flower makes seeds.

blocks.markdown:
A **seed** has a baby plant inside.

A **bulb** stores food to grow a new plant.

When a seed starts to grow, it **germinates**.
blocks.say: Many plants start as a seed. A seed is like a tiny package with a baby plant inside. Some plants start from a bulb instead, like a tulip or an onion. A bulb is a lump with food stored inside it. Both need water and warmth to start to grow. When a seed begins to grow, we say it germinates. Let's watch it.

scenes.caption: A seed.
scenes.say: A tiny seed sits in the soil.

scenes.caption: The seed germinates.
scenes.say: Water and warmth wake it up. A root grows down.

scenes.caption: A shoot grows up.
scenes.say: A shoot pushes up towards the light.

scenes.caption: A new plant.
scenes.say: Soon there are leaves, and a new plant has grown!

question.prompt: What does a seed need to start growing?
question.hint: Think about what you give a plant.
question.explanation: Seeds need water and warmth to germinate.

blocks.title: Plan the cress test
blocks.goal: Put each cup in the right place: Light and water, or No water.
blocks.say: Let's test what a plant needs. We plant cress seeds in three cups. Cup A has light and water. Cup B has water but is in the dark. Cup C has light but no water. Only one thing is different each time. That is called a fair test. Before you look at the cups, make a prediction. Which cup will grow best?

blocks.title: Grow your own cress
instructions: Wet the cotton wool in all three cups and sprinkle some seeds on each.
Cup A: put it on a sunny windowsill and keep it damp.
Cup B: put it in a dark cupboard. Cup C: put it on the windowsill but give it no water.
Look every day for a week and draw what you see.

question.explanation: In a fair test we change only one thing, so we know what made the difference.

points: Seeds and bulbs grow into new plants

A fair test changes only one thing
blocks.say: Remember. A seed holds a baby plant. It needs water and warmth to germinate. In a fair test, only one thing is changed.

blocks.markdown:
Plants need **light**, water, air and space to grow.

A plant without light turns pale and droops.
blocks.say: Growing plants need water from the soil, light from the sun and air around their leaves. They also need room to grow. A plant makes its own food using light. That is why plants on a dark shelf turn pale and droop. Watch what happens to three plants.

scenes.caption: Cup A: light and water. Tall and green!
scenes.say: Cup A had light and water. After a week, the cress is tall and green.

scenes.caption: Cup B: dark. Pale and weak.
scenes.say: Cup B was in the dark. The cress is pale and yellow and floppy.

scenes.caption: Cup C: no water. Dry and brown.
scenes.say: Cup C had light but no water. The cress is dry and brown.

question.explanation: Cress needs light and water to grow well.

options.text: The one with light and water

blocks.markdown:
We **eat** plants, build with them and need them for clean air.

Planting a tree is a kind thing to do.
blocks.say: Plants are everywhere and they help us in so many ways. We eat their fruits, seeds and roots. Wood from trees gives us furniture and paper. Plants make the air we breathe, and give animals food and shelter. Muslims are taught to care for nature and to plant trees, because planting a tree is a good deed. Look at plants in our lives.

blocks.alt: Fruit, vegetables, grain and wood all come from plants.
blocks.caption: Fruit, vegetables, grain and wood all come from plants.
blocks.say: Look at these. An apple, a carrot, wheat grains and wood. They all come from plants.

question.explanation: Bread is made from wheat, a plant.

blocks.title: Plant detective
materials: A plant in a pot, garden or park
instructions: Find a plant and look closely.
Draw it and label the stem, leaves and flower if it has one.
Give it water if the soil is dry.
blocks.say: Be a plant detective at home or in the park. Find a plant and look for its parts. Which is the roots? Which is the leaf? Does it have a flower or fruit? Draw what you see.

blocks.alt: A date palm and a tulip: different plants, same parts.
blocks.caption: A date palm and a tulip: different plants, same parts.
blocks.say: Plants that grow near you in Pakistan or the UK might look different. A date palm grows in hot places, and a daffodil in cooler places. They are all plants with the same parts.
